title: Understanding the HTML Head
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of understanding the html head in a browser document.
Apply at least one relevant rule from this lesson to a small HTML example.
Check the result using browser inspection, a validator, or an accessibility checklist.

content.intro: This lesson turns “Understanding the HTML Head” into a practical authoring skill. You will work with the role of the <head> element, understand the choices that matter, and check the result instead of relying on guesswork.
content.why_it_matters: Meaningful structure and metadata make content easier to navigate, understand, share, and maintain across different devices and assistive technologies.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Meaningful structure and metadata make content easier to navigate, understand, share, and maintain across different devices and assistive technologies.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The head contains document metadata and resource links rather than the ordinary visible page content.

items.title: The role of the <head> element
items.text: The head contains document metadata and resource links rather than the ordinary visible page content.

items.title: Metadata versus visible page content
items.text: Metadata describes the document or its relationship to other resources. Keep each value accurate, unique where appropriate, and consistent with the visible page; search systems may ignore metadata that is misleading.

items.title: The <title> element
items.text: The title gives the document a concise name used by browser tabs, bookmarks, and search result contexts.

items.title: The <meta> element
items.text: Meta provides metadata such as character encoding, viewport behavior, and descriptions.

items.title: The <link> element
items.text: Link relates the document to an external resource, commonly a stylesheet or icon.

items.title: The <base> element
items.text: The <base> element is one of the decisions covered by Understanding the HTML Head. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.

items.title: The <style> and <script> elements at a conceptual level
items.text: Script links or embeds JavaScript; execution timing and trust boundaries matter.

content_blocks.code: Beginner Gardening Guide
content_blocks.expected_output: The title and description provide document metadata; only use the canonical URL if it is truly the preferred public URL.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet in an .html file and open it in a modern browser. Inspect the result, then run an HTML validator if the lesson concerns syntax or structure. Example paths are illustrative; provide the referenced files or adjust paths before evaluating media/resource behavior.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the snippet in this lesson file or paste it into a fresh index.html file, then repeat the check.

content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Prefer the native semantic element that communicates intent. Do not choose markup solely for its default visual style.

content.task: Create a small HTML example that demonstrates understanding the html head. Keep the markup minimal, give every element a clear purpose, and inspect the rendered result.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the relevant concept from Understanding the HTML Head.
Keep IDs unique and use valid nesting.
Check the result in a browser and record one finding.
hints: Start with the smallest valid example for understanding the html head.
Add one element or attribute at a time, then check the result.
Compare the source and rendered DOM if the behavior surprises you.
content.expected_output: The title and description provide document metadata; only use the canonical URL if it is truly the preferred public URL.

troubleshooting.symptom: The expected content does not appear.
troubleshooting.check: Confirm the file was saved with an .html extension and inspect its path and nesting.
Check the resolved URL and confirm the referenced file or external resource exists and allows the request.

troubleshooting.symptom: The page looks correct but the markup may be invalid.
troubleshooting.check: Run the Nu Html Checker and follow its first relevant diagnostic, then validate again.

common_mistakes.why: The default appearance is not the element’s main meaning and can make navigation or maintenance harder.
common_mistakes.fix: Choose the element that matches the content purpose, then use CSS for presentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a browser’s recovery means the source is valid
common_mistakes.why: Browsers often recover from malformed markup, which can hide defects and produce unexpected document structure.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the rendered DOM and run a validator against the original source.

common_mistakes.why: Missing files, narrow viewports, keyboard access, invalid input, or other states can expose defects.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the expected state plus one realistic edge case and an accessibility path.

summary: Understanding the HTML Head is about expressing document structure or behavior intentionally.
Script links or embeds JavaScript; execution timing and trust boundaries matter.
Verify both markup and behavior; do not infer correctness from appearance alone.
